## Requirements: Extract a business-neutral nession-tmux SDK and establish Agent Session domain ownership

### Background / owner decision (2026-10-26)

**Decision:** Treat tmux as an independent Rust infrastructure capability, initially an internal workspace crate named **nession-tmux**, designed to be independently testable and potentially publishable to crates.io. At the same time, make **Session** a first-class Agent domain boundary. This is **not** a rename/move of the existing Agent tmux folder or a WebSocket-only broadcast patch.

The target ownership chain is:

~~~text
Web / CLI / MCP / central-server connection
          -> Agent SessionService / SessionRegistry
             -> SessionTerminalRuntime (lease, input, ordered stream, subscribers)
                -> Agent TmuxSessionBackend adapter (Nession-specific policy)
                   -> nession-tmux (independent tmux library)
                      -> typed Admin/one-shot operations OR persistent TmuxClient
                         -> private tmux server/socket
~~~

**Nonnegotiable:** the independent tmux library must compile and be useful without nession-agent, nession-protocol, nession-common, WebSocket, Claude integration, xterm or a Nession Session definition. Conversely, no Agent domain/gateway module may construct its own tmux process/command outside this library. The SDK is **tmux-native**; Nession's SessionRuntime, ControlLease and stream/replay are separate higher-layer authorities.

**Review baseline:** main @ d68252a68303f57deb4ac2de7b59b894440d93df; staging is a separate integration branch and may contain newer terminal fixes. Re-read the exact integration head before moving code; do not copy old main files over newer staging fixes.

### Verified current-state inventory (source-grounded)

| Current owner | Evidence / gap | Target |
|---|---|---|
| Agent tmux/client/mod.rs | Persistent typed -C/-CC TmuxClient with one ordered source event consumer, pending-command FIFO/tombstones and bounded ingress. Already delivered by #2307/#2380. [Code](https://github.com/BestNathan/nession/blob/d68252a68303f57deb4ac2de7b59b894440d93df/crates/nession-agent/src/tmux/client/mod.rs) | Move implementation into independent nession-tmux; preserve all invariants |
| Agent tmux/cmd.rs | Explicit -S process/socket owner, stale-socket handling, but imports nession_common::tmux_socket and embeds Nession history/config defaults. [Code](https://github.com/BestNathan/nession/blob/d68252a68303f57deb4ac2de7b59b894440d93df/crates/nession-agent/src/tmux/cmd.rs) | Generic, explicitly configured process/socket management in SDK; Nession-specific defaults stay with Agent |
| Agent tmux/ops.rs and client/commands.rs | Typed one-shot argv grammar and Control Mode command encoding are different routes; existing semantic-owner work #991 must not regress. [Ops](https://github.com/BestNathan/nession/blob/d68252a68303f57deb4ac2de7b59b894440d93df/crates/nession-agent/src/tmux/ops.rs), [Control commands](https://github.com/BestNathan/nession/blob/d68252a68303f57deb4ac2de7b59b894440d93df/crates/nession-agent/src/tmux/client/commands.rs) | One operation-semantic owner with transport-specific, testable encoders; no generic arbitrary argv escape hatch |

[Code](https://github.com/BestNathan/nession/blob/d68252a68303f57deb4ac2de7b59b894440d93df/crates/nession-agent/src/tmux/manager.rs) | Generic tmux management API in SDK; Nession create/lifecycle/env policy in SessionService |
| Agent tmux/env.rs / util.rs | tmux operations and Nession sourced-script cleanup / startup helper policy intermixed. [Env](https://github.com/BestNathan/nession/blob/d68252a68303f57deb4ac2de7b59b894440d93df/crates/nession-agent/src/tmux/env.rs) | SDK owns only tmux-native commands; Agent owns environment binding/scripts and errors policy |
| Agent tmux/control.rs / pty.rs | ControlModeSession wraps TmuxClient, source event handoff, capture barrier, window-size guard; legacy plain PTY backend separately supported. [Control](https://github.com/BestNathan/nession/blob/d68252a68303f57deb4ac2de7b59b894440d93df/crates/nession-agent/src/tmux/control.rs) | SDK may expose generic capture/order and tmux-native APIs; Agent adapter owns Terminal stream/ACK policy; preserve legacy backend during migration |
| Agent server/websocket.rs | AttachedSession/SessionMap/peers/lease/stream/input and tmux backend currently in network handler; on last peer removal backend.close is called. attach replaces peer by persistent client_id. [State](https://github.com/BestNathan/nession/blob/d68252a68303f57deb4ac2de7b59b894440d93df/crates/nession-agent/src/server/websocket.rs#L101-L154), [Attach cut](https://github.com/BestNathan/nession/blob/d68252a68303f57deb4ac2de7b59b894440d93df/crates/nession-agent/src/server/websocket.rs#L1026-L1053), [Disconnect](https://github.com/BestNathan/nession/blob/d68252a68303f57deb4ac2de7b59b894440d93df/crates/nession-agent/src/server/websocket.rs#L3815-L3858) | Move into Agent Session registry/runtime; connection lifecycle is not terminal-resource lifecycle |

| Agent runtime.rs | Composition root shared by entrypoints (#1014), but AgentServer still creates its own tmux manager/session map. [Composition](https://github.com/BestNathan/nession/blob/d68252a68303f57deb4ac2de7b59b894440d93df/crates/nession-agent/src/runtime.rs) | Construct/inject one Agent SessionService for all entrypoints and access paths |

**Existing accepted authority, not to reimplement:** #991 tmux semantics; #2307 Control Mode TmuxClient; #575 explicit socket isolation; #1645/#1925 terminal consistency, epoch/seq/atomic cut/replay/ACK; #2286 active-device ControlLease; #1619 shared Agent session streams. #170 (OPEN) separately owns Session Environment Binding semantics. #93 (CLOSED) was an earlier in-Agent tmux-manager refactor and **did not** establish an independent distributable tmux crate or the new Session domain boundary; this is a new owner decision, not re-opening a completed SC.

### Architecture decision A — nession-tmux is a standalone tmux SDK

Suggested structure (names illustrative, invariants binding):

~~~text
crates/nession-tmux/
  Cargo.toml                 # independent 0.x version; initially publish = false
  src/
    lib.rs                  # small stable tmux-native public facade
    config.rs               # explicit binary/socket/config/version/options
    error.rs                # typed errors incl. uncertain execution on timeout
    server.rs               # one-shot administrative client
    operations/             # typed tmux-native operations/targets/parse/result
    client/                 # persistent Control Mode TmuxClient
      mod.rs
      commands.rs
      events.rs
      state.rs
    protocol/               # byte-exact parser/framing
    transport/              # -C pipe, -CC PTY, subprocess/socket
  tests/                    # self-contained fake + real isolated tmux
  examples/                 # manage sessions; attach/watch pane output

crates/nession-agent/src/
  session/
    mod.rs, model.rs, registry.rs, service.rs
    terminal/{runtime,control,subscriber,stream,input,recovery}.rs
    environment/...         # governed by #170
    tmux_backend.rs         # Nession-specific adapter using nession-tmux
  server/...                # transport/auth/protocol adapters only
  runtime.rs               # composition root
~~~

**SDK responsibilities:** tmux server/socket/process configuration and isolation; typed admin operations before any control attachment exists (create/list/kill/set/show env, pane/window queries); a per-attachment persistent TmuxClient for -C/Pipe and -CC/PTY; typed tmux IDs/events; exact byte framing, command-reply matching, timeouts/cancellation, error/source-loss semantics; safe detach/cleanup; testable operation grammar and explicit options. It must expose enough generic API to use on its own with a private socket and no Agent.

**Do not equate every operation with a single persistent Client.** Before the first attach, tmux sessions must still be creatable/listable/killed by an admin client. The Admin and Control Mode executions can have distinct transports/response semantics while sharing one typed tmux-semantic definition where genuinely equivalent; raw pane bytes (send-keys -H) are NOT the same as textual keys/shell-init lines. Never degrade exact command-reply matching or bootstrap cut just to force identical signatures.

**SDK forbidden knowledge:** Nession agent/session IDs and DTOs; nession-protocol/common/runtime dependencies; Claude bindings, memory pressure thresholds, env source-script lifetime, Nession fixed 5000-history product default, JS/xterm, P2P/Relay, ControlLease, SessionStreamState, subscription credit, OutputApplied ACK, Nession protocol wire. Keep any Nession-specific socket resolution/default path in Agent/CLI composition; the SDK accepts explicit validated paths/options and does not silently fall back to the caller's personal tmux socket. Preserve the current safe -S/private-socket execution as an Agent-configured invariant.

**Package/publication policy:** keep the crate internal with publish = false initially, with an independent version rather than inheriting Nession's product version. Avoid dependencies on non-publishable workspace crates and application-private dev fixtures; test the actual packaged dependency graph and usage from a standalone consumer (e.g. from a packaged tarball/temporary external test crate). Provide README, examples, public API docs, explicit supported tmux/platform matrix and licensing decision. The repository currently has no root LICENSE file; do NOT invent a license or publish a crate in this Requirement. Require explicit owner approval + manifest metadata + cargo package and cargo publish --dry-run before any later publication; actual crates.io upload is out of scope.

Upstream references: [tmux Control Mode](https://github.com/tmux/tmux/wiki/Control-Mode), [Cargo publishing](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/publishing.html), [Cargo workspace inheritance](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/workspaces.html), [Cargo publish control](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/manifest.html#the-publish-field).

### Architecture decision B — Session is an Agent domain boundary

**Separate five lifetimes/identities:**

- **Nession Session**: logical work session / desired settings, survives viewer absence; tmux Session is its process resource (may outlive Agent).
- **Agent SessionRuntime / TerminalRuntime**: Agent-process resource owner; at most one current TerminalRuntime per Session key; owns ControlModeSession/TmuxClient, stream/input states, ControlLease and subscription registry. This is NOT the Web-side SessionRuntime (#1309).
- **TmuxClient attachment generation**: each underlying Control Mode attachment/replacement is distinct; source-loss is not subscriber drop.
- **Physical Connection**: ephemeral WebSocket connection, with authenticated principal separate from identity and no persistence requirement.
- **Subscription**: ephemeral per-connection/per-Session membership, its own subscriber-generation, ACK/issued credit, outbound queues and cleanup token. A controller lease is tied to the authorized current subscriber and separately generation-fenced.

The single Agent SessionService/Registry must be assembled by runtime.rs and shared by P2P + central Server connector + any CLI/MCP/internal entrypoints. WebSocket handlers may authenticate/validate a contract and call Session methods; they must NOT mutate a SessionMap, instantiate a tmux backend, run tmux commands, or choose stream/control policy. Other capabilities (Files/Git) do not automatically become Session state merely because they share the Agent.

**Transition contract:**

~~~text
create Session -> session service validates policy -> SDK admin create -> materialize Session runtime as needed
first Terminal attach -> get_or_init exactly one backend/TmuxClient and ordered source consumer
A subscribe -> A receives output; authorized meaningful activation may acquire lease
B subscribe -> A and B both receive identical source stream; B is observer until active takeover
B foreground/explicit interaction -> ControlLease g2; broadcast role change; only B input/authoritative resize
A foreground later -> ControlLease g3; both continue receiving output; stale g1/g2 mutations rejected
A disconnect -> remove only A's subscription; B's subscriber, backend and stream remain
last subscriber disconnect -> unsubscribe only; do not implicitly kill tmux Session or conflate client absence with source loss
new connection -> new connection/subscription IDs; resume only from verified stream/applied cursor or truthful bootstrap
explicit Session kill -> cancel subscriptions/tasks, close matching attachment, kill only correct tmux Session, cleanup Nession env resources
tmux source loss -> retire matching attachment generation, report explicit loss; replace attachment/epoch by stated recovery policy
Agent restart -> restore tmux Session discovery; new in-memory stream/input epochs and truthful continuity status
~~~

**No unbounded idle pool:** session runtime lifetime is Agent-owned, not per-WebSocket. Define an explicit per-session active/idle resource policy (including CPU/memory limits, bounded stream history, whether/how idle attachments are retired and continuity becomes unproven). A deliberate idle retirement MUST be distinguishable from WebSocket disconnect; if output was not retained, reconnection cannot claim uninterrupted replay.

**Identity and compatibility:** audit all uses of persistent client.auth client_id before modifying it. Do not blindly remove a shared identity needed by nonterminal auth/session correlation. For Terminal membership, use Agent-issued opaque connection/subscription identities independent for same-origin tabs; Release/ACK/Detach must target the exact subscription token/generation, not an old logical client_id that may be reused. ControlLease takeover still follows #2286 meaningful activation (not passive resize/reconnect). Strict generation fencing must be rolled out with versioned protocol compatibility; current authorize_mutation(None) legacy tolerance must not silently defeat the new strict path.

**Ordered stream & fanout:** one tmux source-event consumer, one Session stream epoch/seq owner and producer/subscribe atomic cut; all observers receive byte-identical output and correctly ordered authoritative resize with bounded independent per-subscriber queues/ACK/credit. Preserve parser-applied ACK, capture cut vs VT fidelity distinctions, stale callback fencing and P2P/Relay parity; resize latest-level coalescing (#2388) and aggregate byte handoff (#2387) must not reintroduce source blocking. Do NOT add a competing tmux/xterm VT emulator, replay log or protocol owner.

**Environment:** #170 owns changing Nession Session Environment Binding, including eliminating attach-time mutation; this architecture must make the Session-owned path possible and must not move Nession env scripts into the SDK. Do not silently mark #170 as completed by relocating files.

### Dependency/API guardrails

- Only nession-tmux may construct tmux processes and encode tmux command grammar (all production routes, including session watcher/central connector/CLI and legacy PTY paths). Update the existing tmux-socket-isolation checker and negative fixtures to the new owner rather than deleting or bypassing it.
- Only Agent SessionService owns Session lifecycle; TerminalRuntime owns ControlLease/stream/input and bounded Subscriber state; transport adapters and Web UI do not.
- nession-tmux cannot import/reference any Nession-internal workspace crate or wire type, including test-only dependencies; no ambient global Agent socket/config requirement for an independent SDK consumer.
- Preserve explicit -S, TMUX/TMUX_TMPDIR scrubbing, safe child reap (no destructive kill-server/default-socket), -C/-CC parity, byte-for-byte non-UTF8, command FIFO/tombstones, capture source order, source-loss and admission deadlines.
- Keep one per-session mutation serialization authority across P2P/Relay as in #961/#1021; no map lock held across backend I/O and no orphaned forwarders after replacement.
- If protocol fields evolve, use nession-protocol versioned contracts/codegen/Gates (#678), test mixed versions and enforce exact identity/generation authorization; do not embed new wire schemas in the SDK.

### Non-goals

- Publishing to crates.io in this Issue (future owner decision, independent work); no licensing presumption.
- Changing Terminal product UX, screen appearance or xterm renderer; no AI Workspace/UI prototype.
- Reworking #170 environment business semantics or redoing already accepted terminal consistency logic.
- Adding multi-pane/window product behavior, a generalized workflow/Channel framework or durable exact-once terminal input.
- Replacing all existing backends in one destructive PR; preserve legacy plain PTY path until regression parity justifies retirement.

### Migration and review slices (separate focused PRs; do not merge one giant refactor)

| Slice | Change and proof boundary | PR base |
|---|---|---|
| 0 / architecture inventory | Freeze ownership matrix, call-site inventory (including runtime/watchers/CLI), public SDK API, active/idle policy, migration/compatibility and supported tmux version matrix; update one canonical docs/architecture owner and scoped AGENTS references | main if docs-only |
| 1 / SDK extraction | Create independent crate with explicit config + generic socket/process, move typed Control Mode parser, transports, commands, events and self-contained tests; keep Agent behavior unchanged through adapter | staging |
| 2 / SDK admin convergence | Move TmuxCmd/TmuxOps and all native create/list/kill/env/capture/resize operations behind typed SDK API; remove duplicate argv/raw spawn; update safety Gate, fake process tests, real tmux API examples | staging |
| 3 / Agent Session boundary | Extract SessionService/Registry/TerminalRuntime and move AttachedSession/control/stream/input/subscriptions out of websocket.rs; one resource owner from runtime.rs for both routes | staging |
| 4 / lifecycle + identity | Separate socket vs subscription vs lease; persist tmux Session independently; per-connection ephemeral Terminal subscribers; exact attach/detach/cleanup, multi-tab broadcast, PC-phone takeover, source-loss and restart semantics | staging |
| 5 / hardening | Independent packaged consumer check, API docs/tests, real-tmux -C/-CC/macOS/Linux proofs, selected end-to-end fault Cases, protocol compatibility, no stale old owner, deployment unchanged | staging |

### Prototype

- Decision: Not needed.
- Reason / interaction uncertainty: internal crate/API/Agent state ownership only; existing PC/mobile Terminal interactions remain governed by #2286.
- Status: Not needed.


**Case coverage plan:** add source-aligned Cases under e2e/acceptance/cases/2469/SC-01, SC-02, SC-03, SC-06, SC-07, SC-08 and SC-09 as appropriate. Cases bind the exact merged staging SHA, tmux version, supported OS and P2P/Relay session evidence. Slice PRs carry source-level witnesses but do not claim pre-merge Case projection: the Acceptance machinery evaluates `method: agent` criteria pre-merge and projects Cases only from merged-SHA runs. No main-only or production-deployed property has been identified; do not impose a universal Full E2E gate on individual slice PRs. **Verification tier: integration (L2)** because this is a cross-crate + lifecycle migration with real multi-client/source-loss boundaries, not a release or security-policy cutover.

**Plan note (2026-10-26):** the original plan declared `method: case` criteria `when: pr`. Pre-merge Case records are evidence-only in this repository — the pre-merge gate requires every `when: pr` criterion to be Pass, and Cases are projected only from merged-SHA runs (the same unexecutable combination repaired for #2300 in #2318). Because this Requirement lands in six slices, all criteria now prove at the merged `staging` SHA; slice PRs carry their source witnesses and the `method: agent` criteria are reviewed on staging. No criterion text or evidence bar changed.

### Success Criteria

- [ ] SC-01 nession-tmux builds, tests and documents as a standalone reusable Rust library (including packaged/external-consumer fixture); its dependency graph, code, and test support contain no Nession business crate/DTO or Agent-only initialization.
- [ ] SC-02 A real isolated tmux server can be created/listed/managed before attach and interacted with afterward through typed SDK APIs; every tmux process/command in Nession production paths goes through the SDK and continues explicit private-socket isolation without a raw-spawn bypass.
- [ ] SC-03 On supported real macOS/Linux tmux, -C Pipe and -CC PTY preserve typed byte-exact non-UTF8 output, command FIFO/error/tombstones, capture/live cut, lifecycle/source-loss, resource bounds and graceful cleanup; unsupported variants fail explicitly rather than silently falling back.
- [ ] SC-04 SDK accepts explicit tmux configuration while Nession's current socket resolution, history limit, Claude/env defaults, memory checks and protocol contracts stay in Agent/CLI; no change in effective existing deployment defaults.
- [ ] SC-05 One Agent-wide SessionService/Registry is the sole writable owner shared across P2P and central/Relay paths, and no WebSocket handler directly holds/mutates Session state or instantiates/executes a tmux client.
- [ ] SC-06 Last subscriber removal, reconnect, backend replacement, Agent shutdown and Session kill each have distinct generation-safe cleanup; no unintended tmux Session termination, hidden leak, false stream continuity or old forwarder writing into a new attachment.
- [ ] SC-07 Same-origin browser tabs and separate devices independently subscribe and receive broadcast; only the most recently meaningfully active authorized peer controls input/resize, A→B→A takeover fences stale frames/cleanup and passive reconnect does not take over.
- [ ] SC-08 Under output bursts, slow observers, bootstrap and P2P↔Relay route changes, subscribers share one Agent stream timeline and truthful applied-ACK/replay/checkpoint semantics; memory/queues remain bounded and a healthy observer is not stalled by another peer.
- [ ] SC-09 Import/ownership/socket/protocol guards and documented owner paths detect new illicit SDK→Nession dependencies, raw tmux spawns, unauthorized state mutation or incompatible wire changes, without weakening established quality gates.
- [ ] SC-10 The internal package has independent version and publish=false, third-party-facing README/examples/API docs and packaging checks; actual crates.io publication is not attempted and license/registry readiness remains an explicit later authorization.
